practiceQuestions.q: Practice Question 1: What is the mathematical requirement of a Simple Majority under the Indian Constitution?
opts: More than 50% of the total strength of the House
More than 50% of the members present and voting
Not less than 2/3 of the members present and voting
More than 50% of the effective strength of the House
practiceQuestions.sol: Explanation for Practice Question 1: A simple majority is also known as an ordinary majority. It requires more than 50% of the members of the House who are present and voting (excluding abstentions).

practiceQuestions.q: Practice Question 2: The removal of the Speaker or Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha requires which majority?
practiceQuestions.sol: Explanation for Practice Question 2: Under the Constitution, the Speaker of Lok Sabha is removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the House, which is defined as an Effective Majority (more than 50% of total strength minus vacancies).

practiceQuestions.q: Practice Question 3: Which of the following is passed by a Simple Majority in the Parliament?
opts: Removal of the Chief Election Commissioner
practiceQuestions.sol: Explanation for Practice Question 3: Money bills, ordinary bills, financial bills, no-confidence motions, and confidence motions are all passed by a simple majority of members present and voting.

practiceQuestions.q: Practice Question 4: What is the required majority in Rajya Sabha for passing a resolution to create a new All-India Service under Article 312?
opts: Special Majority of 2/3 of members present and voting
practiceQuestions.sol: Explanation for Practice Question 4: Under Article 312, Rajya Sabha can pass a resolution declaring the creation of a new All-India Service necessary in national interest by a special majority of not less than 2/3 of members present and voting.

practiceQuestions.q: Practice Question 5: The impeachment of the President of India under Article 61 requires which majority?
opts: 2/3 of members present and voting AND absolute majority of the House
2/3 of the total strength of the House
Effective majority in both Houses of Parliament
practiceQuestions.sol: Explanation for Practice Question 5: Impeachment of the President under Article 61 requires a special majority of not less than 2/3 of the total sanctioned strength of the House. This is the strictest majority requirement in the Indian Constitution.

mockTestQuestions.q: Mock Question 51: Which majority is required to approve the continuation of a National Emergency under Article 352?
opts: Simple Majority of members present and voting
Special Majority under Article 368 (2/3 of present & voting AND absolute majority)
Special Majority of 2/3 of total strength of the House
mockTestQuestions.sol: Explanation for Mock Question 51: Originally, a simple majority was sufficient, but the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1978 changed it to require a Special Majority (Type 2: 2/3 present and voting + absolute majority) to approve or extend a National Emergency.

mockTestQuestions.q: Mock Question 52: When a Constitutional Amendment Bill seeks to alter the representation of states in Parliament, what is the required approval?
opts: Special Majority under Article 368 + ratification by more than half of the State Legislatures by simple majority
Simple Majority in Parliament + ratification by 2/3 of states
Special Majority of 2/3 of total strength in Parliament only
mockTestQuestions.sol: Explanation for Mock Question 52: Amending federal provisions (like representation of states in Parliament under the Seventh Schedule or Article 368 itself) requires a Special Majority under Article 368 (Type 2) followed by ratification from more than half of the state legislatures by simple majority.

mockTestQuestions.q: Mock Question 53: If a House has a total sanctioned strength of 250, with 10 vacant seats, 200 members present, and 20 members abstaining from voting, what is the minimum votes required for a Simple Majority and an Effective Majority?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Explanation for Mock Question 53: 1. Present and voting = 200 present - 20 abstaining = 180 voting. Simple majority requires > 50% of 180 = 91 votes. 2. Effective strength = 250 total - 10 vacancies = 240. Effective majority requires > 50% of 240 = 121 votes.
